name.text: Construct the derivative line of a quadratic (INNODEMS)

questiontext.text:
The blue curve is \( f(x) = {@fexpr@} \).

Move the \(x\)-slider to slide the red point \(A\) along the blue curve. At each position you see the tangent to \(f\) there, and a green point whose height is the slope of that tangent — that is, \( f'(x) \), the derivative at that \(x\). (The green point leaves no trail.)

Your task: drag the two purple points \(P\) and \(Q\) to draw the straight line that the green slope-value lies on for every \(x\). That line is the graph of the derivative \( f'(x) \).

[[jsxgraph input-ref-ans1="ref_ans1" input-ref-ans2="ref_ans2" width='560px' height='560px']] var mm = {#m#}, kk = {#k#}, aa = {#float(a)#}, cc = {#c#}; var win = {#win#}, xslider_mid = {#float(xslider_mid)#}, xslider_dist = {#float(xslider_dist)#}, yinit = {#yinit#}; var f = function (x) { return aa*x*x + kk*x + cc; }; // the curve var fp = function (x) { return mm*x + kk; }; // its derivative (target line) var board = JXG.JSXGraph.initBoard(divid, { boundingbox: [-win, win, win, -win], keepAspectRatio: true, axis: true, showCopyright: false, showNavigation: false, pan: {enabled: false}, zoom: {enabled: false} }); // f(x): the blue parabola. Its arms may run off the board - that is fine. board.create('functiongraph', [f, -win, win], {strokeColor: '#0055bb', strokeWidth: 2, highlight: false, name: ''}); board.create('text', [-win + 0.3, win - 0.6, 'y = f(x)'], {color: '#0055bb', fontSize: 14, fixed: true}); // An x-slider drives A along the curve. A slider handle drags smoothly regardless of // scaling (a glider on the curve does not), and reads well: "sweep x, watch the slope". // Sits in the bottom-left, just above the tangent-slope readout. var xs = board.create('slider', [[-win + 0.5, -win + 1.8], [-win + 4.5, -win + 1.8], [xslider_mid-xslider_dist, xslider_mid, xslider_mid+xslider_dist]], {name: 'x', snapWidth: 0.01, precision: 1, baseline: {strokeColor: '#bbb'}, highline: {strokeColor: '#d32f2f'}, label: {fontSize: 15}}); var xv = function () { return xs.Value(); }; // A = (x, f(x)), driven by the slider (not draggable). var A = board.create('point', [function () { return xv(); }, function () { return f(xv()); }], {name: 'A', size: 2, strokeColor: '#d32f2f', fillColor: '#d32f2f', fixed: true, showInfobox: false, label: {offset: [8, 14], color: '#d32f2f', fontSize: 13}}); // Tangent through A with the true slope f'(A.x). board.create('line', [A, [function () { return A.X() + 1; }, function () { return A.Y() + fp(A.X()); }]], {strokeColor: '#d32f2f', strokeWidth: 1.5, dash: 2, straightFirst: true, straightLast: true, highlight: false}); // Green slope-point at (x, f'(x)) and a dashed drop to the axis. board.create('point', [function () { return xv(); }, function () { return fp(xv()); }], {name: '', size: 2, strokeColor: '#2e7d32', fillColor: '#2e7d32', fixed: true, showInfobox: false}); board.create('segment', [[function () { return xv(); }, 0], [function () { return xv(); }, function () { return fp(xv()); }]], {strokeColor: '#2e7d32', strokeWidth: 1, dash: 1}); board.create('text', [-win + 0.3, -win + 0.7, function () { return 'tangent slope at x = ' + xv().toFixed(1) + ' is ' + fp(xv()).toFixed(1); }], {color: '#2e7d32', fontSize: 13, fixed: true}); // The student's answer: two purple points forming a line var P1 = board.create('point', [-2, yinit], { name: 'P', size: 2, strokeColor: '#8e24aa', fillColor: '#8e24aa', showInfobox: false, label: {offset: [6, 12], color: '#8e24aa'} }); var P2 = board.create('point', [2, yinit], { name: 'Q', size: 2, strokeColor: '#8e24aa', fillColor: '#8e24aa', showInfobox: false, label: {offset: [6, 12], color: '#8e24aa'} }); board.create('line', [P1, P2], {strokeColor: '#8e24aa', strokeWidth: 2, straightFirst: true, straightLast: true}); stack_jxg.bind_point(ref_ans1, P1); stack_jxg.bind_point(ref_ans2, P2); [[/jsxgraph]]
[[input:ans1]] [[validation:ans1]] [[input:ans2]] [[validation:ans2]]

generalfeedback.text:
The graph of \(f'\) plots the slope of the tangent to \(f\) at each \(x\). Because \(f\) is a quadratic, those slopes change at a steady rate, so the graph of \(f'\) is a straight line — and a line needs only two points, both of which you can read straight off the picture.

1. Find where the gradient is zero. The tangent is horizontal at the vertex of the parabola, here at \(x = {@vertex_x@}\). A horizontal tangent has slope \(0\), so the graph of \(f'\) passes through \[ \left({@vertex_x@},\ 0\right). \]

2. Read one more tangent. Slide \(A\) to \(x = {@wsx2@}\) and read the height of the green point — the slope of the tangent there is \({@wsslope2@}\). So \(f'\) also passes through \[ \left({@wsx2@},\ {@wsslope2@}\right). \]

Plot those two points and draw the straight line through them: that is the graph of \(f'\). Every other tangent slope falls on the same line, so \[ f'(x) = {@m@}x + {@k@}. \]

Here is the finished picture. The parabola's tangent is horizontal at the vertex (red), which drops straight down to the green point \(\left({@vertex_x@},\,0\right)\) on the \(x\)-axis; the purple line through the two green points is \(f'\):

[[jsxgraph width='420px' height='420px']] var mm = {#m#}, kk = {#k#}, aa = {#float(a)#}, cc = {#c#}; var vx = {#vertex_x#}, wx2 = {#wsx2#}, ws2 = {#wsslope2#}; var win = 8; var f = function (x) { return aa*x*x + kk*x + cc; }; var fp = function (x) { return mm*x + kk; }; var b = JXG.JSXGraph.initBoard(divid, {boundingbox: [-win, win, win, -win], keepAspectRatio: true, axis: true, showCopyright: false, showNavigation: false, pan: {enabled: false}, zoom: {enabled: false}}); // the parabola f, with its horizontal-tangent vertex b.create('functiongraph', [f, -win, win], {strokeColor: '#0055bb', strokeWidth: 2, highlight: false}); b.create('text', [-win + 0.3, win - 0.6, 'y = f(x)'], {color: '#0055bb', fontSize: 13, fixed: true}); b.create('point', [vx, f(vx)], {size: 3, strokeColor: '#d32f2f', fillColor: '#d32f2f', fixed: true, showInfobox: false, name: ''}); b.create('line', [[vx - 1.4, f(vx)], [vx + 1.4, f(vx)]], {strokeColor: '#d32f2f', strokeWidth: 1.2, dash: 2, straightFirst: false, straightLast: false, highlight: false}); b.create('segment', [[vx, f(vx)], [vx, 0]], {strokeColor: '#999', strokeWidth: 1, dash: 1}); // the derivative line f' (the correct answer) b.create('functiongraph', [fp, -win, win], {strokeColor: '#8e24aa', strokeWidth: 2.5, highlight: false}); b.create('text', [vx + 2.2, 2*mm + 0.8, "y = f '(x)"], {color: '#8e24aa', fontSize: 13, fixed: true, anchorX: 'left'}); // the two points read straight off the picture b.create('point', [vx, 0], {size: 4, strokeColor: '#2e7d32', fillColor: '#2e7d32', fixed: true, showInfobox: false, name: '(' + vx + ', 0)', label: {offset: [8, -4], fontSize: 12}}); b.create('point', [wx2, ws2], {size: 4, strokeColor: '#2e7d32', fillColor: '#2e7d32', fixed: true, showInfobox: false, name: '(' + wx2 + ', ' + ws2 + ')', label: {offset: [8, 8], fontSize: 12}}); [[/jsxgraph]]

Notice the constant \(c = {@c@}\) played no part: sliding the whole parabola up or down doesn't tilt any tangent, so it never changes \(f'\).

node.description: Degenerate: are the two points stacked vertically (same x)?

truefeedback.text: Your two points \(P\) and \(Q\) are stacked vertically (the same \(x\)), so they don't define a slope. Drag them apart horizontally so the line runs left-to-right.

node.description: Does the line run through the parabola's vertex? Checked first, so it fires as soon as the line hits the vertex, whatever the slope.

truefeedback.text: Your line runs through the vertex of the parabola. The gradient there really is \(0\) — but on the graph of \(f'\) a slope of \(0\) means a height of \(0\), so that point belongs on the \(x\)-axis, at \(\left({@vertex_x@},\,0\right)\), not up at the turning point. Anchor your line there, on the axis, then check its steepness against the green slope-heights.

node.description: Is the slope of the student's line correct (= m)?
Slope correct - is the intercept correct (= k)?

truefeedback.text: Correct — your line passes through the tangent-slope value at every \(x\), so it is the graph of \(f'\). For a quadratic, those slopes fall on a straight line.

node.description: Slope wrong - is it a instead of 2a (dropped the factor of 2)?

truefeedback.text: Close — the right idea, but your line is too shallow, by half. Sample a few tangents with the slider and watch the green point: its height changes twice as fast as your line does. Read two green slope-heights carefully and steepen your line to pass through them.

falsefeedback.text: Your line's slope doesn't match the tangent slopes. Drag the red point \(A\) to a few different \(x\)-values and watch the green point — those green heights are what your line must pass through. Remember you are plotting the slopes of \(f\), not the curve \(f\) itself.

node.description: Slope ok, intercept wrong - did they use the constant term c?

truefeedback.text: Your slope is right, but the line is shifted vertically — it looks like you read the intercept off the parabola (its height \(c\) at \(x=0\)) instead of off the tangent. Sliding \(f\) up or down doesn't tilt any tangent, so \(c\) has no effect on \(f'\). Move \(A\) to \(x=0\) and read the green point: that height is where \(f'\) crosses the axis.

falsefeedback.text: Your slope is right, but the line crosses the \(y\)-axis in the wrong place. Move the red point \(A\) to \(x = 0\): the height of the green point there is \(f'(0)\), which is exactly where your line should cross the axis.

qtest.description: Correct: two lattice points on f'(x)=mx+k.
Correct via a DIFFERENT pair of points on the same line.
Degenerate: both points at the same x.
Half-slope: line of slope a (=m/2) instead of 2a. (On rare variants where this slope-a line also happens to pass through the vertex, it is reported as prt1-vertex - run on another variant.)

Used c: correct slope but intercept = c. (On variants where the vertex sits on the y-axis, k=0, or k=2m, this same line also passes through the vertex and is reported as prt1-vertex - run on another variant.)
Correct slope, generic wrong intercept (not c, not k).
Generic wrong slope (horizontal line at y=7, clear of every possible vertex height, so it lands on slopewrong not vertex).
Through the vertex: correct slope, but the line passes through the parabola's vertex (vertex_x, yvertex) rather than (vertex_x, 0).
